Progress rail

.dr-node · --done · --now · .dr-rail · --at2 · --zone · __step · __lbl · __lbl--now · components/progress.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

  • Accepted
  • En route
  • On‑site
  • Done
  1. 1.dr-railA 4-column grid. The track runs behind the circles from the centre of column 1 to the centre of column 4 (12.5% to 87.5%), --line for the rail and green for the walked span.
  2. 2.dr-node--doneA finished milestone: green fill and border, charcoal check, 9.46:1.
  3. 3.dr-node--nowThe live milestone: green border, a filled charcoal dot and a 4px halo of green at 20%.
  4. 4.dr-rail__lbl--nowThe live label steps from slate 10.5/400 to charcoal 10.5/600, so the state is carried by glyph, weight and position, never colour alone.
  5. 5li:last-child .dr-nodeA pending milestone: 22px circle, 2px --line border on --card, no glyph.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: (.dr-node, .dr-rail) — the order card's rail and the tracking timeline.

When to use

The rail answers the question the client asks most between payment and arrival: where is my order now. It closes the void RJ-C2 names, so it stands wherever a live order is shown: the active card on order-history and the top of tracking and its -aerial / -inspection variants. One node component serves both, where two class names once drew the same circle.

The milestones are the canonical four everywhere: Accepted · En route · On-site · Done. Labels are one or two words, the user's words for where the order is, never equipment terms. On‑site takes a non-breaking hyphen so the shortest label cannot break and shift the rail. aria-current="step" marks the live step programmatically, so WCAG 1.4.1 is met by glyph, weight and position.

DESIGN.md also describes a vertical axis on tracking (a 2px connector at left:10px). No class for it is declared in components/, and tracking draws the horizontal rail, so it is not shown here.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Progress · voice.md P1, P4 · kit.html "One node, two axes" · CLAUDE.md RJ-C2

Rule and anti-rule

Do

  • Accepted
  • En route
  • On‑site
  • Done

The four milestones of one live order, with the current one marked by aria-current="step", its own dot and a heavier label.

Don’t

  • Service
  • Details
  • Pay
  • Track

The rail as a checkout stepper. It tracks the order's milestones and nothing else; a rail that counts form steps teaches the client that the four nodes mean something other than where the operator is. The ordering flow is three taps and needs no stepper. For a position among slides, use the pager.
